Hi Alice / Rajesh —

Quick technical notes ahead of the deep-dive. I’ll prepare slides on audit logs and TTLs as requested. High-level options and recommendations: 

1) Recommended: Service accounts + short-lived JWTs (server-to-server)
   - Create a Redwood service account for each FinTechCo application (staging/prod)
   - Use signed JWTs to mint short-lived access tokens (1–15m TTL depending on latency/SLOs)
   - Store long-term private keys in your KMS (AWS KMS) and sign requests from your backend; Redwood validates signatures and issues ephemeral tokens if desired
   - Benefits: least-privilege, easier rotation, good auditability

2) Alternative: Managed API keys with strict constraints
   - Use rotating API keys (per service) with IP allowlists and per-key scopes (read/embeddings/write)
   - Rotate via automation (recommended 30–90 day rotation window) or offload to your secrets manager

3) Embeddings & reranker keys
   - We recommend separate keys/scopes for embeddings and model inference to minimize blast radius (embeddings keys can be limited to vector write/read only).

4) KMS integration and HSM
   - Redwood can accept signed JWTs from your KMS-backed keys (we do not require you to share raw key material).
   - For customer-managed keys at rest, we support integrating logs and attestations; we can discuss HSM/KMS proofing in the deep-dive.

Example Node SDK flow (server-to-server, signed JWT -> exchange for ephemeral token):
// pseudocode
const jwt = require('jsonwebtoken');
const fs = require('fs');
\const privateKey = fs.readFileSync('/path/to/key.pem'); // ideally from KMS
const payload = { iss: 'fintechco-service-a', aud: 'redwood', sub: 'service-a' };
const token = jwt.sign(payload, privateKey, { algorithm: 'RS256', expiresIn: '5m' });
// exchange for Redwood token
const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/token/exchange', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
  body: JSON.stringify({ jwt: token })
});
const data = await res.json();
const ephemeral = data.access_token; // use for subsequent API calls


Curl example (managed API key, short-lived):
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $EPHEMERAL_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-3.1", "input":"..."}'

Operational recommendations:
- Issue per-service service accounts and rotate private keys via KMS.
- Prefer TTL < 15m for tokens used in high-risk flows; longer TTLs are OK for backend-to-backend high-throughput jobs with IP restrictions.
- Configure audit logging and set alerts on auth failures and anomalous token usage.

I’ll bring a couple of example flows and our rotation checklist to the meeting. If you can share any existing network ACLs or proxy details, that helps.
